policy.strategy: approved-baseline, two-sided: non-regression below, bounded improvement above
policy.reapproval:
Re-approved 2026-08-15 for the `daemon adapter` entry only: lines 41.84 -> 44.56, functions 35.88 -> 39.15. Functions is the one that failed — +3.27 points, over the 3.0 improvement slack — and lines moved +2.72, inside it; both are moved together because an entry re-approved on one metric and stale on the other is the half-corrected ruler this policy was written to stop. Measured at 763687cc on macos-aarch64 with cargo-llvm-cov 0.8.5, working tree clean.

Numerator and denominator both grew, which is what an upward move has to show: functions 1480 -> 1553 (+73) with covered 531 -> 608 (+77), lines 16713 -> 17671 (+958) with covered 6992 -> 7875 (+883). Coverage rose because the added code is reached by tests, not because exclusions widened — none did.

The movement is **not** attributable to one commit and is not credited to one. Five commits touched crates/daemon since the previous approval at 15f54289 (FR-167's delete audit, FR-169's vanish watcher, FR-170's artifact ownership, the db status archive fix, and 763687cc, which replaced the identity comparison in both lifecycle guards after CI measured it inoperative on Linux). Per this file's own rule, attribution is a reason to credit the improvement in the record rather than a reason to leave the ruler wrong — so it is recorded here and moved.

Re-approved 2026-08-12 for FR-165 requirement 3, which made the comparison two-sided. Three entries move: CLI (lines 35.49 -> 53.02, functions 30.82 -> 54.94), cli/commands (33.78 -> 44.78, 27.8 -> 38.68) and daemon/session (15.52 -> 20.69, 32.81 -> 37.68). Every other entry is left alone because its drift is inside the 3.0-point slack: core/domain +0.98/+0.95, daemon adapter +1.09/+1.25, and twelve pairs at exactly 0.00. Measured at 15f54289 with the revision and the tracked-Rust digest recorded before and after the run, both unchanged. 

This reverses the reasoning of the 2026-08-02 note, deliberately and with the reason stated. That note saw CLI at 52.86% against an approved 35.49% and declined to move it: 'that movement belongs to the FRs that caused it, and this run is not their evidence.' The 2026-07-27 note had recorded the same gap. The principle is sound and the consequence was not: attribution is a reason to credit the movement to another FR in the record, not a reason to leave the ruler wrong, and leaving it wrong cost the ability to detect a regression. With approved at 35.49 and actual at 53.02, CLI coverage could have fallen seventeen points and the gate would have stayed green -- a one-sided ratchet does not merely fail to reward improvement, it discards the regression detection it exists for. Two notes a week apart observing the same gap and changing nothing is what made this a requirement rather than an annotation. 

The 52.86% those notes recorded does not reproduce: the second derivation is 53.02% at this revision, on a denominator that grew 7373 -> 7456. Neither number was wrong -- the earlier one was measured before commits that added CLI code -- which is the argument for pinning a revision to every coverage figure, since the same entry legitimately reads differently a week apart. 

Tauri Rust (9.42%) and tauri/commands (5.45%) are unchanged, at exactly 0.00 drift, and are deliberately not exempted: see 'tauriLift' below.
policy.improvementSlackRationale: 3.0 points, and the number comes from the shape of the measured distribution rather than from what would make today green. Measured at 15f54289 (macos-aarch64, cargo-llvm-cov 0.8.5, 22 metric pairs): twelve pairs drifted exactly 0.00, four between +0.95 and +1.25, two between +4.87 and +5.17, and four between +10.88 and +24.12. The interval (1.25, 4.87) is empty, so a band inside it is stable against small perturbations in either direction — moving it a point changes which entries fail only if the distribution itself changes. 3.0 sits in that gap, nearer the incidental side so the check errs toward asking rather than tolerating: it is about 2.4x the largest drift that came from unrelated work and about 1.6x below the smallest deliberate gap. A band of 5.0 was rejected because it splits daemon/session across its own two metrics (lines +5.17 fails, functions +4.87 passes), and a rule that treats one module's two measurements differently is a rule fitted to a number rather than to a property.
policy.tauriLift: Tauri Rust sits at 9.42% lines / 7.73% functions and tauri/commands at 5.45% / 3.47%, the lowest measurable surfaces in the workspace, and FR-165 requirement 3 asked for either a lift plan or a named exemption. Neither is written here as a number, because both would be a guess: no work in FR-165 touched this code, and a target chosen without having tried to test it is the kind of figure the governance-expansion boundary in DD-172 exists to refuse. What is recorded instead is the measurement and the reason it is low: crates/gui is a Tauri command layer whose functions are #[tauri::command] entry points reached through the Tauri runtime, and the workspace has no in-process harness that can invoke them -- the same shape as daemon/source_connection before FR-157, which went 12.21% -> 85.51% once a fixture could reach it, and which was low for the same reason: not hard to test, never entered. The two-sided ratchet now applies to these entries like any other, so the first real lift is caught and re-approved rather than accumulating silently. Deciding the target belongs to whoever builds that harness.
